thesis.core: The AI-compute revenue inflection is real, but earnings quality is not yet commensurate with the rerating. H1 revenue reached RMB906.9m and high-performance computing revenue RMB507.5m, yet attributable profit was only RMB16.8m, operating cash flow was -RMB651.4m, inventory rose to RMB786.6m and short-term borrowings to RMB1.78bn. The 22 September RMB1.67bn GPU-card contract is a procurement contract rather than disclosed downstream sales.
thesis.variant_wedge: The market is capitalizing rapid AI-compute revenue growth as if it already proves durable earnings power. Current disclosures instead show a low-margin, working-capital-intensive hardware ramp financed heavily with short-term debt, while the newest material contract increases procurement exposure without naming a downstream customer or disclosed sales commitment.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Use 2026E normalized EPS bear/base/bull RMB0.10/0.50/1.20. Base assumes H2 revenue scaling and better absorption but still modest net margin; bull requires rapid sell-through of GPU inventory, sustained gross margin and materially improved cash conversion.

operating_and_financial_quality.judgment: Revenue growth is genuine, but profit conversion, operating cash flow and financing quality remain weak relative to the scale of the rerating.

capital_and_event_update.judgment: The procurement agreement supports supply availability but does not by itself evidence sell-through, customer credit quality, pricing, net margin or cash conversion.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: H1 attributable profit was only RMB16.8m despite RMB906.9m revenue. Base assumes H2 scale-up with modest net-margin recovery; bull requires a major improvement in sell-through, financing cost and working-capital conversion.

catalysts: Disclosed downstream AI-compute sales contracts or prepayments validate sell-through of GPU inventory.
H2 operating cash flow turns positive while inventory and receivables growth normalizes.
Short-term debt declines materially despite continued AI-compute revenue growth.
High-performance computing gross margin and company-level net margin improve enough to support materially higher normalized EPS.
kill_thesis: GPU procurement and inventory continue to expand without matching disclosed downstream demand or customer cash collection.
Operating cash flow remains deeply negative while short-term borrowing rises further.
High-performance computing gross margin falls materially below the current mid-teens level or Q3/Q4 profit conversion remains near break-even.
Receivables, inventory and financing costs grow faster than sustainable gross profit.
